# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-threading

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **Message Board / Threading** in isolation on the 10-pair `core` subset with `vertex_ai/gemini-3-8-flash` (`high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter, `$40` cost cap). Outgoing messages receive monotonic run-scoped IDs (`m1`, `m2`, ...) with `--reply-to <id>` and `--resolve` flags, an active open-thread footer on every turn, and a harness-pinned active thread board preserved across 28K context compactions. Compared against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-stepcounter` (4/10 passed, 2 merge conflicts).

## Observations

- Passed 3/10 (`dottxt_ai_outlines_task/1655`, `openai_tiktoken_task/0`, `pallets_jinja_task/1621`) with 2 merge conflicts (`react_hook_form_task/153` and `typst_task/6554`; same-function overlap pair `dspy_task/8563` merged cleanly, improving over the baseline conflict there).
- Zero command-parse errors occurred across 222 messages (12 explicit thread roots opened and resolved, 184 per-turn `[Open threads (...)]` reminders), and step-limit stops fell from 7/20 in the baseline to 3/20.
- However, without explicit speech-act intents (`Proposal` / `Request` vs. `FYI`), generic thread bookkeeping increased context compactions from 82–100 to 116 (`$14.62` total cost) without improving functional pass rate (`typst_task/6554` diverged into a merge conflict instead of reconciling).
